merger_name: Healthe Care – Knox Private, Ringwood Private, Northpark Private, Victorian Rehabilitation Centre and Geelong Clinic
merger_description:
Healthe Care Group Pty Ltd (**Healthe Care**), through its wholly owned subsidiaries, proposes to acquire 5 private hospital assets in Melbourne and Geelong from Healthscope entities (the **Acquisition**).

As part of the Acquisition, Healthe Care will acquire the following hospitals:

* Knox Private Hospital in eastern Melbourne;
* Ringwood Private Hospital in eastern Melbourne;
* Northpark Private Hospital in north-east Melbourne;
* The Geelong Clinic, a mental health hospital in Geelong; and
* The Victorian Rehabilitation Centre, a rehabilitation facility in eastern Melbourne.

The Acquisition forms part of a broader consortium acquisition of Healthscope's portfolio. The other consortium members are Calvary, Acurio Health and KnG Group, which will each acquire separate hospitals pursuant to inter-conditional sale agreements. In addition to its acquisition of the five Healthscope assets located in Melbourne and Geelong, and as part of the consortium proposal, Healthe Care proposes to acquire substantially all the assets of Prince of Wales Private Hospital in Sydney. The proposed acquisition of that hospital is subject to a separate notification (MN-60052).

Healthe Care is an Australian private healthcare group that operates 17 private hospitals and day surgeries across New South Wales, Victoria and Tasmania. Healthe Care is a majority owned by funds managed or advised by Pacific Equity Partners, a private markets fund manager.

In Melbourne, Healthe Care currently operates one private hospital, Mulgrave Private Hospital (located in eastern Melbourne), and two Hobson specialist day surgeries in Sydenham and Werribee (located in north-west and south-west Melbourne, respectively).

Healthscope is Australia's second-largest private hospital operator. On 26 May 2025, Healthscope's parent entities entered into receivership, with McGrathNicol appointed as Receivers to complete a sale of the business. The Receivers conducted an extended sale process over Healthscope's hospital portfolio.

events.title: Healthe Care – Knox Private, Ringwood Private, Northpark Private, Victorian Rehabilitation Centre and Geelong Clinic - Phase 1 determination

determination_table_content.details: The reasons for the ACCC’s determination are set out in section 2.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the interests of consumers.

For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines and interim merger process guidelines. Determination | Healthe Care – Knox Private, Ringwood Private, Northpark Private, Victorian Rehabilitation Centre and Geelong Clinic (MN-25058)

In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered the information and documents that were submitted with the notification form, additional information provided by the parties to the Acquisition, information provided by third parties and market feedback.
For the reasons given below, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into effect.
Background on voluntary administration of Healthscope and consortium acquisition

In May 2025, Healthscope’s parent entities went into voluntary administration, and receivers (Receivers) and administrators were appointed by its lenders and the Healthscope Board respectively to conduct an orderly sale of the hospitals in its network. The Receivers conducted an extended sale process over Healthscope's hospital portfolio.

The Acquisition forms part of a broader consortium acquisition of Healthscope's portfolio, following the Receivers’ sale process. The other members of the consortium are Acurio Health, Calvary and KnG Group, which each propose to acquire separate hospitals pursuant to inter-conditional sale agreements.

In addition to its acquisition of the five Healthscope assets located in Melbourne and Geelong, and as part of the consortium proposal, Healthe Care proposes to acquire substantially all the assets of Prince of Wales Private Hospital in Sydney. The proposed acquisition of that hospital is subject to a separate notification (MN- 60052).

Healthe Care (through Mulgrave Private Hospital) overlaps with Knox Private Hospital and Ringwood Private Hospital in the supply of private hospital services in eastern Melbourne and surrounding areas, specifically:

items.text: the supply of medical, surgical and emergency care services across a range of medical specialties to patients;
the supply of private hospital facilities, equipment and support staff to visiting medical officers (VMOs); and
the supply of Hospital Purchaser Provider Agreements to private health insurers.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: The ACCC considers there is no material overlap between Healthe Care’s existing hospitals and the other Target Hospitals (i.e. Northpark Private Hospital, Victorian Rehabilitation Centre and Geelong Clinic).

The ACCC has considered the effects of the Acquisition by comparing the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition proceeds against the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition does not proceed. Determination | Healthe Care – Knox Private, Ringwood Private, Northpark Private, Victorian Rehabilitation Centre and Geelong Clinic (MN-25058)

The ACCC has considered whether the Acquisition is likely to substantially lessen competition in the supply of private hospital services to patients, VMOs or private health insurers in eastern Melbourne and surrounding areas.

For the purpose of its assessment, it was not necessary to reach a definitive view on the precise product or geographic boundaries of the relevant market, as it does not materially alter the ACCC’s competition assessment.

The ACCC considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the supply of private hospital services to patients, VMOs or private health insurers in eastern Melbourne and surrounding areas.
Based on information provided by the Parties and by third parties, the ACCC makes the following findings:

items.text: Post-Acquisition, there will still be multiple alternative suppliers of private hospital services in eastern Melbourne and surrounding areas.
There is no real commercial likelihood of an alternative purchaser acquiring the Target Hospitals.

In the absence of a commercially realistic alternative purchaser, and in the context of Healthscope’s voluntary administration, there is not a real prospect that the Target Hospitals would continue operating as private hospitals in the future without the Acquisition.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: Accordingly, the Acquisition is unlikely to result in a substantial lessening of competition relative to the future without the Acquisition.
